findings.reason: the node would dispatch with a negative control that raises instead of showing the defect, and would discover only after writing the fixture that the plan's simulation cannot produce an older-declaration arm.
findings.text: the done-when fixes the simulation as "patching `QUERY_KEYS`, `_RUNS_COLUMNS` and `_STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION`", but those constants are precomputed at import (`_RUNS_UPDATE`, `_RUNS_INSERT`, `_query_values` all close over `QUERY_KEYS` at module load, run_store.py:127-146), so patching the three globals leaves the SQL arity at the current declaration and the base arm dies before touching the backfill: `sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Incorrect number of bindings supplied. The current statement uses 9, and there are 8 supplied.` (measured at a32f36a239 on a 50-row store). The declared control — "at the base revision, case (a) runs the row backfill over all 500 rows" — is therefore unreachable as written; what the base arm must exhibit is the whole-store rewrite, and the node cannot choose its own way to synthesise the subset declaration while the plan names a patch set.

findings.reason: the node's only red-at-base measure is satisfied at base by the mechanism already in the tree, so the gate cannot distinguish the new trigger from the old one.
findings.text: the negative control "at the base revision, case (a) requests no reload" is false for the case the test describes: at base `ReloadWindow.due` returns true whenever `newest != self.running` (follower_reload.py:194-197), and the admission loop feeds it `_admit_code_stamp()` at every pass boundary and re-execs when it is due (admission/service.py:305-330); `fleet_supervisor` restarts a declared service whose recorded stamp differs from the checkout's current stamp (fleet_supervisor.py:1775-1801). A boundary where the running code holds A and the code on disk holds B already requests a reload at base, so the arm either fails its control or must be built to suppress the existing trigger — which is the behaviour under test.

findings.reason: as written the node builds a second trigger for a case the tree already covers, so its gate proves nothing the code stamp does not already do, and the plan should either name the real gap (the store outrunning a service whose own tree is stale, where reloading cannot help and the fix is the operator-visible refusal) or drop s85.
findings.text: the Why's claim that "nothing ties a reload to the one change that makes running code wrong about shared state" is contradicted by the code it cites: any commit touching `reckon/run_store.py` moves the checkout's code stamp, the running image's stamp then differs from the on-disk one, and the pass-boundary window reloads on exactly that difference. The one state the stamp cannot see — the store ahead of both the running and the on-disk code — is the state the Deliverable deliberately leaves running with a logged line. So the reload condition the Deliverable adds (store version differs and the on-disk code already carries it) is a strict subset of the existing trigger, and the evidence offered for the gap (no admission pass 02:27Z–04:11Z) is a reload-boundary defect already fixed at 658ee9d230, not a missing schema-version tie.
